nodes.summary: Allele frequencies at the first locus are unchanged by random mating (for every real `r`).
nodes.title: Recombination preserves first-locus allele frequencies

nodes.summary: The frequency `∑ b, x (a, b)` of allele `a` at the first locus.
nodes.title: Allele frequency at the first locus

nodes.summary: Allele frequencies at the second locus are unchanged by random mating (for every real `r`).
nodes.title: Recombination preserves second-locus allele frequencies

nodes.summary: The frequency `∑ a, x (a, b)` of allele `b` at the second locus.
nodes.title: Allele frequency at the second locus

nodes.summary: The recombination fraction is always below `1/2` (for every real `d`).
nodes.title: Haldane's recombination fraction is below one half

nodes.summary: Every `r < 1/2` is the recombination fraction at the distance `-½ log(1 - 2r)`. The hypothesis keeps `log` on positive arguments: at `r = 1/2` the right side would use the junk value `log 0 = 0`. The distance is nonnegative exactly when `0 ≤ r`.
nodes.title: Every recombination fraction below one half is attained

nodes.summary: Haldane's map function is nonnegative at nonnegative distances.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of Haldane's map function

nodes.summary: Haldane's map function `r(d) = (1 - e^{-2d}) / 2`: the recombination fraction between two loci at map distance `d` Morgans when crossovers form a Poisson process (no interference).
nodes.title: Haldane's map function

nodes.summary: The probability that a Poisson count of mean `d` is odd, as a series: `∑_{k odd} e^{-d} d^k / k! = (1 - e^{-2d}) / 2` (Haldane 1919). The series identity holds for every real `d`; it is a probability for `0 ≤ d`.
nodes.title: Series for the probability of an odd Poisson count

nodes.summary: After `t` generations, `D_t = (1 - r)^t D_0`.
nodes.title: Linkage disequilibrium after $t$ generations

nodes.summary: Linkage disequilibrium decays by the factor `1 - r` per generation: `D' = (1 - r) D` (for every real `r`).
nodes.title: Linkage disequilibrium decays by the factor $1 - r$

nodes.summary: The linkage disequilibrium `D = x_AB x_ab - x_Ab x_aB`.
nodes.title: Linkage disequilibrium of a two-locus gamete law

nodes.summary: The inverse map function `d = -½ log(1 - 2r)` recovers the map distance.
nodes.title: Inverse Haldane map function recovers map distance

nodes.summary: Haldane's map function (Haldane 1919): if the number of crossovers in an interval of map length `d` Morgans is Poisson with mean `d`, the probability of an odd number of crossovers, i.e. of recombination between the ends of the interval, is `(1 - e^{-2d}) / 2`.
nodes.title: Haldane's map function from Poisson crossovers

nodes.summary: The classical form of the recursion: coupling gametes (`AB`, `ab`) lose `r D` and repulsion gametes (`Ab`, `aB`) gain `r D`. This identity holds for every real `r`; the biological domain is `0 ≤ r ≤ 1/2`.
nodes.title: Classical form of the recombination recursion

nodes.summary: Recombination keeps gamete frequencies nonnegative for `0 ≤ r ≤ 1`.
nodes.title: Recombination preserves nonnegativity of gamete frequencies

nodes.summary: One generation of random mating with recombination fraction `r`: `recombine r x g = (1 - r) x_g + r p_{g.1} q_{g.2}`.
nodes.title: Random mating with recombination

nodes.summary: Recombination keeps gamete frequencies summing to `1`.
nodes.title: Recombination preserves total gamete frequency

nodes.summary: Loci far apart are unlinked in the limit: `r → 1/2` as `d → ∞`.
nodes.title: Distant loci are unlinked in the limit

nodes.summary: Linkage disequilibrium tends to `0` whenever `0 < r ≤ 1`; this contains the biological range `0 < r ≤ 1/2`. For `r = 0` (complete linkage) `D` is constant.
nodes.title: Linkage disequilibrium tends to zero
